fixer.title: ci: run Agent Host E2E tests in their own job

introducer.title: test: run Agent Host E2E as its own test unit in GitHub Actions and ADO

cases.mechanism: Agent Host E2E launched up to five test processes but the entire suite was sequenced before the Electron integration subprocess in one runner job, so integration could not start until the E2E suite completed.
cases.symptom: PR Windows / Electron checks that selected Agent Host E2E spent roughly 15 additional minutes on the serial critical path (about 37.5 minutes total per the traced workflow scenario), with analogous smaller delays on Linux and macOS.
cases.fixedBehavior: The Agent Host E2E subprocess suite now runs on a separate Windows runner in parallel with Electron integration tests, removing its approximately 15-minute suite duration from the serial Windows Electron critical path; the required check still joins both results.
cases.evidence: In the base workflow, blame line 233 identifies the Agent Host E2E step introduced by e886b81b9b9d4a39d8e397c33e76ce04d5cbbe85. The base diff shows that this 30-minute subprocess suite ran in the same Windows reusable-workflow job immediately before `test-integration.bat`, whose condition explicitly allowed it to proceed after the E2E step. The PR adds `windows-agent-host-e2e-tests` as a distinct reusable-workflow invocation and passes `integration_tests: false`, while the existing Electron job no longer enables Agent Host E2E, so the two runner jobs can execute concurrently.
